title: Launch Threshold Guardian — weekmap and incident script (2026-09)
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, actionable Weekmap + Incident Script for the ‘threshold guardian’ release (small-sprint feature set). Goal: get to safe 100% traffic in one business day with clear watch windows and an officer-of-the-hour rota. Use this when we need fast rollout but want well-defined escape hatches.

High-level constraints / assumptions
- Release size: config + routing + two small runtime PRs (no schema changes).
- Backwards-compatible: clients will fallback to previous routing if telemetry signals hit thresholds.
- Telemetry baseline: current median p95 latency = 210ms, error rate = 0.12%.
- Business day target: 09:00 start, fully backfilled by 18:00 if no major signals.

Quick TL;DR checklist (one-line actions)
- Preflight: smoke branch deployed to staging, smoke tests green, load profile run at 1.5x baseline.
- Pre-announce: #deployments channel 24h + 1h and include SRE on-call.
- Launch: start 5% cohorts -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% (gates between phases).
- Watch: 45 minute watch after each step, run targeted latency/error dashboards.
- Rollback: if p95 latency increases > 30% OR error rate > 0.5% OR any customer-impacting alerts, roll back to previous router config.

Detailed preflight (owners and tickets)
- Code freeze snapshot created (owner: Marco) — PRs merged: #4872, #4884, #4890. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4872.
- Staging deploy complete and annotated (owner: Jenna). Smoke results attached to ticket JIRA:RINF-3120.
- Load run (owner: Diego) — ramp script: small-cohorts.json, 1.5x sustainable TPS run for 20 minutes, check tail latencies and queue depth.
- Canary config prepared: routing policy file v2-threshold-guard.yaml, stored in S3: s3://deploy-configs/threshold-guard/2026-09-14.
- Rollback doc: quick commands added to runbook (CLI snippet, console toggles).

Weekmap (hour-by-hour plan)
Day 0 (D-1)
- 09:00 — Final checklist sign-off. Owners on deck: Marco (release lead), Jenna (staging/rollout ops), Diego (telemetry), SRE on-call named in Slack thread.
- 12:00 — Deploy smoke to staging + run long smoke (30m).
- 15:00 — Dry-run rollback; validate roll-forward and roll-back automation.
- 17:00 — Pre-announce to customers (if required) and post deployment windows.

Day 1 (Launch day)
- 08:00 — Final sync (10m), confirm observability dashboards up, traces and synthetic checks green.
- 09:00 — Start cohort A: route 5% traffic. Note: keep feature gates live.
- 09:45 — Watch window (45m). Tasks: check p95, error counts, saturation, new traces for uncaught exceptions. If metric red -> rollback.
- 10:00 — If green, move to cohort B: 20% traffic.
- 10:45 — Watch (45m). Run step-regression smoke prompts (short scripted calls) to validate model outputs for a small prompt set.
- 11:00 — If green, move to cohort C: 50% traffic.
- 11:45 — Watch (45m). Run load-synthesis with ephemeral clients to detect resource exhaustion.
- 12:30 — Midday quick sync (5–10m). Note any partial anomalies, escalate if > 2 high signals.
- 13:00 — If green, move to 100% traffic.
- 13:45 — Watch (60m). After this window, shift to reduced monitoring cadence (see below).
- 15:00 — Post-launch note to #deployments summarizing status and any tickets opened.
- 18:00 — Hand off to standard day watch, update deployment log and close shift.

Escalation and rollback thresholds (hard gates)
- Latency: p95 > baseline * 1.30 for a sustained 3 consecutive minutes -> immediate pause and investigate. If sustained for > 10m, rollback.
- Errors: total 5xx spike to > 0.5% of requests in watch window -> rollback.
- Telemetry anomaly: sudden drop in KV cache hit rate > 10pp -> pause.
- Quality regression: automated prompt-set scoring drops by > 6 points (team metric) -> pause and triage.
- Any Sev1 page -> immediate rollback.

Incident script (officer-of-the-hour playbook)
- Officer role: owns initial triage and first decision (pause vs rollback).
- Step 1 (0–3m): Acknowledge page in PagerDuty, post a short note in #deployments-status with current cohort and observed metric.
- Step 2 (3–10m): Run quick checks: recent deploys (git SHA), host CPU/GPU spikes, queue backlog. Attach relevant graphs.
- Step 3 (10–30m): If root cause uncertain, revert router to previous config (CLI: redwood-deploy route rollback --id <id>) and notify SRE channel.
- Step 4 (>30m): Post-mortem ticket created (owner: release lead). If rollback occurred, capture samples of failing traces and top 10 requests by latency.

Observability checklist (dashboards and alerts)
- Primary dashboards: ReleaseGuard-Latency, ReleaseGuard-Errors, ReleaseGuard-KVCache, ReleaseGuard-ModelQA.
- Synthetic probes: 5 steady probes hitting common endpoints at 30s cadence.
- Tracing: enable debug sampling for one request path (sample rate 1%).
- Logs: tail routing service logs with filter: ERROR or WARN + latency > 500ms.

Release notes draft (to be edited for customer update)
- Summary: Small rollout to improve routing resilience and add a threshold-aware fallback that reduces caller-exposed latency during stress.
- Highlights: New routing policy (v2-threshold-guard) that automatically favors cached model variants under high KV miss conditions. Minor runtime perf improvements for batching logic.
- Impact: No API changes. Expected behavior: more stable tail latency; rare automatic fallbacks during extreme load.
- Rollout plan: gradual cohort ramp over launch day; immediate rollback policy in place.
- Known gaps: We are still validating small prompt-edge cases (prompt set A). If customers notice subtle output variance, please file support ticket and include example.

Open questions / TODOs (owner tags inline)
- Is SLO hop for model-serving documented for this rollout? (Marco)
- Add one more synthetic probe target for embeddings route (Jenna)
- Confirm KMS rotation window doesn't collide with D+1 maintenance (Diego)
- Finalize customer-facing blurb (Comms) — draft waiting in /comms/drafts/threshold-guard.md

Cutover commands (quick reference)
- Promote router: infra-cli router promote --config s3://deploy-configs/threshold-guard/2026-09-14 --env prod
- Rollback router: infra-cli router promote --config s3://deploy-configs/threshold-guard/previous --env prod
- Pause traffic: infra-cli router throttle --percentage 0 --reason "pause"

Post-launch retro (30/90 day checkpoints)
- 30d: telemetry deep-dive — did p95 tail improve? owner: Diego.
- 90d: review fallback economics — did fallbacks materially increase cost? owner: Product-Optimize.

Notes to reviewers (quick)
- This is intentionally concise; designed to be pasted into Slack #deployments and used as the canonical launch day script. Feel free to comment inline on thresholds that feel aggressive.
- I want a second pair of eyes on the quality gating (prompt set scoring) — it’s the riskiest automated signal right now.

Revision history
- 2026-09-14: initial sketch (Aisha)
- 2026-09-16: added rollback CLI, load run notes (Diego)
- 2026-09-20: tightened latency gate and added synthetic probe checklist (Jenna)

Attachments / artifacts to add before finalizing
- long-smoke-results-2026-09-14.log (staging)
- small-cohorts-ramp.json (ramp config)
- prompt-set-A.csv (scoring set)

End of doc — keep short, actionable.
